lens: Bloomberg-terminal density: multi-pane data cockpit for power users and managers
name: Night Desk Cockpit
one_liner: A dark, keyboard-first trading-desk cockpit for live coaching and scoring, with a repo-native persona library that any contributor can extend.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed Bloomberg density for the working surfaces (practice, live, debrief, progress, team): multi-pane, tabular numerics, keyboard-first, dark by default. Changed it for the landing page and library so the README stays readable. Mobbin's closest matches: Dialpad's call panel and coaching hub, Writer's filter-rail agent library, and the Emergent and Gorgias wizards. Firecrawl was rate-limited, so competitor claims come from vendor-blog search snippets and are unverified. Self-scores (brief scale): A 8, B 7.5, C 7.5, D 6.5 (only if cues land under about 1.5s), E 5.5 (needs 150+ seeded personas; 3.5 at today's three), F1 6 (hosted team tier, crowded market), F2 6 (open core lowers enterprise trial friction), F3 3 (worth building).

palette.use: Primary actions and selected rows (keeps brand blue)
Score up, goal met (keeps the teal accent)
Chips naming the AI model in use; no OpenAI logo or brand green
Light theme background and landing page

design_language.typography: Geist 600 for headings with -0.02em tracking (28/20/16px). Geist 400/500 for body at 14px and 13px in dense tables. Geist Mono with tabular-nums for scores, timers, timestamps and transcript line numbers.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 6px radius on panels and inputs, 10px on landing cards only. 1px hairline borders. Depth comes from stepped surface tones, not blurred shadows or gradients. 2px primary focus ring.
design_language.motion: Panel and inspector slides 150ms ease-out. Score bars tween 300ms. Cue card slides in from the right in 160ms and stays at least 6s unless dismissed. No fade-up entrance on data. prefers-reduced-motion removes all tweens.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react, 16px in dense panes and 20px elsewhere, 1.5 stroke. One custom cue glyph (amber dot on a short bar) marks coach messages.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default across the app. Landing page and README hero render readable in light. Both themes use the same :root tokens with a data-theme override and a toggle; first visit follows prefers-color-scheme.

navigation_and_ia: Left rail replaces the glass header: a 56px icon rail that expands to 216px on hover or pin, with Practice, Library, Progress, Team (manager role only) and Settings, plus a model-status chip at the bottom. The top bar carries breadcrumbs and the Ctrl+K palette across personas, scenarios and past calls. Routes: /library, /library/new (wizard), /practice/[scenario] (pre-call), /practice/[id]/live, /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. Keyboard first: J/K move, Enter starts, M mutes, C toggles coach, E opens End with confirm, ? shows shortcuts. Saved layouts: Rep and Manager. Mobile: bottom tab bar (Practice, Library, Progress, More) with Start call as the primary action.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Two model paths run in parallel and never share context. The persona runs on OpenAI Realtime (voice) or chat completions (text). The coach reads each finished turn and emits at most two cues as strict JSON (next question, objection alert, talk-track step, filler warning). Cues appear as amber text only and never enter the persona's session, so the persona cannot hear coaching. The grader updates rubric scores every turn with transcript-line evidence, reusing the existing evidence-backed grader. Target: a cue within about 1.5s of the turn ending; otherwise it moves to the debrief. Unassisted mode hides cues but still scores, for certification runs. Each cue is logged with whether the rep used it and the score change that followed, which feeds the debrief.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: the repo ships a persona pack, one validated JSON or YAML file per persona (zod schema, checked in CI), grouped by job: SDR cold call, AE discovery, insurance, mortgage, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections. Filters: job, industry, difficulty, objection type, channel, source. Launch target: 150+ personas across 20+ jobs, with the rest sourced from contributors. Wizard: five steps, one question at a time, with Auto-answer. Inputs: job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP text or a pasted call. Output: the same schema, streamed into a live persona card, then a 60-second dry-run call before save. Export writes the file for a pull request.
signature_moments: Cue dock: whispered amber cues the persona never hears, each logged for adoption and score change.
Rubric tape: five criteria bars that tick every turn, with evidence pins into the transcript.
Replay timeline in the debrief: the score line plus cue and objection markers on the call clock.
Persona card that fills in live while the wizard streams structured output.
Models-in-use footer that names each OpenAI model in the call and shows its live latency.
openai_fund_angle: Models shown, not hidden: every call footer names the models in use (Realtime voice, coach, grader, wizard), and the landing page carries a 'Powered by OpenAI models' line in the style of the 'Powered by OpenAI' badge on Codecademy's voice-interview screen. No OpenAI logo or brand green is used, so nothing implies endorsement. Codex invitation: AGENTS.md at the repo root; CONTRIBUTING has a one-click 'Ask Codex to add a persona' prompt; a good-first-issue board reads GitHub labels; a persona-author wall credits contributors. Program fit: the landing page shows maintainer activity (release, CI, contributor count). Official terms say benefits are discretionary and verified, so the README makes no dollar promises; the $25K figure is a third-party claim.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1: tokens in tailwind.config (dark default, Geist), shadcn primitives behind the existing class names, cockpit shell with rail and Ctrl+K. Phase 2: live call three-pane layout, cue dock and coach path, behind a feature flag. Phase 3: persona library, wizard and the persona pack; migrate localStorage scenarios into 'Mine'. Phase 4: debrief timeline, progress and team views. Keep Next.js 15 and Tailwind 3 for now (Tailwind upgrade as a separate change). Do not change the grader's JSON contract. Coach pipeline is backend work and is scoped separately from the UI.

risks: Bloomberg density can overwhelm first-time reps: offer a Simple view and a first-run tour, and keep dense layouts off the landing page.
Cues slower than about 1.5s become noise: fall back to post-turn cues and say so in the UI.
Coach text leaking into the persona's session would break the realism the product sells: keep a separate channel and add a test that the Realtime session never receives coach text.
Contributor-written personas will vary in quality: enforce the zod schema, a rubric linter and a review checklist before the 150-persona launch target.
OpenAI fund figures ($25K cap, rolling review, no threshold) come from secondary sources; official terms say benefits are discretionary and need verification.
Competitor claims come from vendor blogs and search snippets; Firecrawl was rate-limited, so no primary competitor pages were read.
shadcn/ui Tailwind 3 support and Geist via next/font were not checked against current docs in this run.
Amber cue text and muted dark-mode labels need WCAG AA contrast checks before adoption.
